races.title: State Assembly, District 25
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Ash Kalra
cands.bio: Democrat from San Jose who has served in the California State Assembly since 2016. Earlier he served on the San Jose City Council. He is a former Santa Clara County deputy public defender and a law professor at Lincoln Law School and San Jose State University.

controversies.text: San Jose Councilman Ash Kalra was arrested for drunken driving on May 7, 2011, after a stop for a broken taillight. He called it a "terrible error in judgment" and apologized to his council colleagues. In June 2011 he pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor. His sentence included three years of probation, a fine, a DUI class and community service.

endorsements.text: For the 2026 race, Ballotpedia lists endorsements from the Democratic Party of California, Working Families Party, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association, SEIU Local 521, California Environmental Voters, Equality California, Our Revolution and YIMBY Action.

cands.gaps: We found no documented actions or statements by Kalra on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, donor-money pledges, police pay and pensions, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys for 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026, so there are no self-reported positions from that source. We found no documented stances on data centers or development, and no foreign ties. The pages we had did not give his birthplace beyond Toronto or any detail on his parents' careers. Sponsored-bill details were not readable on the page we had.

local.label: Roots 80: He was born in Toronto, his family settled in San Jose in 1978, and he attended San Jose public schools and has lived in San Jose ever since.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He has served in the California State Assembly since 2016 and on the San Jose City Council for two terms. He worked as a Santa Clara County deputy public defender for 11 years and as a law professor, and served as a San Jose planning commissioner.
qual.why: He has about a decade of prior state legislative service plus local elected office and a law career, which fits the high band for writing law and the budget. Committee chair roles were not counted.

cands.name: Himat Singh Bainiwal
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 25 in 2026. Attorney who says he has represented individuals and local businesses, and who currently serves as a Historic Landmarks Commissioner, according to his campaign site.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California, Reform California, and several voter-guide groups listed by Ballotpedia (April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide, The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn).

cands.gaps: We found no independent confirmation of his law career, his birthplace or upbringing, or when his Historic Landmarks Commission service began. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. His campaign site gives only general issue statements. We found nothing on his positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no news coverage, controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign website says he was born and raised in San Jose and has family roots across Santa Clara County; this is a self-description and no independent record was found.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Attorney who says he has represented individuals and local businesses; serves as a Historic Landmarks Commissioner (an appointed commission). No elected office or legislative or budget work was found.
qual.why: Law practice fits the middle band for lawyers. The landmarks commission seat adds nothing. No legislative service was found, and the legal career is self-reported and unverified.
